# Pandamonium v1.0.50

This release completes the JOS protocol program. An enforcement-parity suite
now proves every mounted protocol rule has a live owner, and a deterministic
benchmark reports the mounted packs and budget compliance for each scenario.
It also removes an import cycle that could break standalone entry points,
corrects protocol pack budgets and enforcement pointers to their measured
owners, and stabilizes a CI-flaky workspace browser check.

The protocol mount itself — core packs, duty packs by intent, operator
controls, and the JOS-P7 trace — shipped in v1.0.48. v1.0.50 lands the
parity/benchmark certification, the operator documentation, and the follow-up
fixes that close the MAD-784 umbrella.

## MAD-893 — Protocols 4/4: enforcement parity, benchmark, and documentation

### Problem

The JOS protocol packs declared `enforcement` owners and token budgets in their
manifests, but nothing verified that those owners existed or that the shipped
bodies fit their budgets. One manifest pointed at a module that does not exist
(`src/memory_provenance.py`), two core packs exceeded their declared budgets,
and `src/model_context.py` imported `core` at module load, creating an import
cycle for standalone scripts and entry points that load the module first.

### Implementation

`tests/test_protocol_parity.py` now asserts that every shipped pack declares at
least one enforcement owner, that every referenced module imports, that every
JOS protocol has a versioned pack, and that the pack scopes are exactly
`core` + `duty`. `scripts/protocol_benchmark.py` renders the mount for trivial
chat, shell, web-research, and calendar scenarios and reports mounted packs,
declared versus measured body tokens, rendered protocol tokens, and render
scaffolding, failing on real budget drift. JOS-P3 now points at its real
owners (`src/tool_policy.py`, `src/tool_schemas.py`), JOS-P0/JOS-P1 budgets were
raised to their measured values, and `src/model_context.py` resolves its
catalog store path and atomic writer lazily.

### Product value and UI visibility

Every mounted rule is now provably enforced by a module that ships, and the
prompt-budget cost of the protocol layer is measured rather than assumed. The
benchmark shows protocol blocks at 621 tokens (trivial chat) to 1,180 tokens
(web research), including 91–148 tokens of render scaffolding, with every
measured pack body at or under its declared budget.

### Verification

`tests/test_protocol_parity.py`, `tests/test_protocol_duty_packs.py`,
`tests/test_model_catalog_persistence.py`, and `tests/test_protocol_controls.py`
pass, the benchmark reports `status: pass`, and the full Python suite passed
(5,666 passed, 5 skipped) on the merged tree.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No schema, authentication, or dependency change. The benchmark's live-model
comparison (tool selection, completion, latency across a local and a reference
model) remains operator-run; the stub mode is deterministic and CI-safe.

## CI stabilization

The `m7-codex-workspace` Playwright spec waited the 5-second default for the
workspace browser to appear after the picker refresh. Loaded CI runners
repeatedly exceeded that while the same check passes locally in about three
seconds; only that expectation now allows 15 seconds.

## Documentation

`docs/jos-protocol-runtime-status.md` documents the mounted pack layer: core
and duty mounting, the evidence-priority strip under context pressure, the
JOS-P7 mount trace, operator controls, diagnostics, model-aware budgets, and
the parity and benchmark gates.
